deities: Lord Shiva as Mukteshwar ('giver of salvation') - white marble Shiva linga with copper yoni

history.dynasty: None documented (legend attributes origin to the Pandavas; one source claims a 350-year heritage - weakly sourced, verify)
history.period: Antiquity unknown (called 350 years old by local sources; legend places it in the Mahabharata era - conflicting, verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Nainital town - it stands in Mukteshwar town, about 49 km from Nainital, in Nainital district, at about 2,312-2,315 m in the Kumaon hills. Dedicated to Lord Shiva as Mukteshwar, it enshrines a white marble Shiva linga with a copper yoni plus idols of Vishnu, Brahma, Parvati and Ganesha, and is counted among the eighteen most important Shiva temples by some traditions (weakly sourced - verify). Legend says the Pandavas built it during their 12-year exile to seek mukti (salvation), and that Shiva killed a demon here, granting him salvation - hence the name Mukteshwar. Local sources call it a 350-year-old heritage temple; another claims over 5,000 years (dates conflict - verify; no documented dynasty). It is also a noted viewpoint: Nandakot, Nanda Ghunti, Trishul and Nanda Devi are visible on clear days, and the nearby Chauli-ki-Jali cliffs are used for rock climbing. Documented with the corrected location.

name: Mukteshwar Temple
town: Mukteshwar (CSV town 'Nainital' is approximate - the temple is in Mukteshwar town, ~49 km from Nainital)
town_description: Mukteshwar, at about 2,285-2,315 m in the Kumaon hills of Nainital district, is a quiet hill town of orchards, coniferous forests and colonial-era cottages, known for Himalayan views of Nanda Devi, Trishul and Panchachuli. Beyond the temple it is popular for trekking, rappelling and rock climbing at Chauli-ki-Jali; the Indian Veterinary Research Institute's hill campus is nearby.

travel.railway: Kathgodam Railway Station - about 64-73 km (sources vary).
travel.road: About 49 km from Nainital by motorable road (approx. 1.5 hours); taxis and buses run from Nainital, Haldwani and Kathgodam.

visitor_information.best_time: March to June for pleasant weather and clear Himalayan views; visit in all seasons except the July monsoon, which can be tricky.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict: 5:00 AM - 7:30 PM, 6:00 AM - 7:00 PM, and 6:00 AM - 6:00 PM are all cited (verify locally). No entry fee; morning aarti around 6:30 AM per one source.
